newsitem.title: ITALY: Zanussi head said in bid for Olivetti PCs.
newsitem.headline: Zanussi head said in bid for Olivetti PCs.

text.p: The chairman of white goods group Zanussi, Gianmario Rossignolo, has joined forces with U.S. businessman Edward Gottesman in a bid to acquire the PC division of Olivetti, an Italian newspaper reported on Tuesday.

Milan business daily Il Sole 24 Ore said Rossignolo, who apart from heading Zanussi -- owned by Sweden's Electrolux -- has independent business interests, could tip the scales in favour of Gottesman's Centenary Group.

A spokesman for Olivetti declined to comment on the report. The heavily indebted information technology group has said that it is seeking buyers for its PC division which has been squeezed by intense competition from U.S. and Asian manufacturers.
Olivetti's share price rose on the Il Sole report on Tuesday and was trading at 569 lire in mid-morning, up 21 lire from a Friday close of 547.1 lire.

Centenary had already signed a declaration of intent and lawyers were already working on a contract of sale for the PC business, Il Sole said, adding that both parties were hoping to finalise the deal by the end of January.

The report said Rossignolo would probably be the non-executive chairman of an Italian company that would be constituted to take charge of Olivetti's PC interests. Olivetti has a large PC plant at Scarmagno in northwest Italy.
It was not yet clear whether Rossignolo intended to acquire a stake in the venture, Il Sole added.
U.S. corporate debt trader Gary Klesch, who runs London-based Klesch and Co, is also reported to have expressed an interest in taking over the Olivetti PC business.
